answer: One concrete defense is a slashable stake bond: every agent locks tokens before it can transact, and peers attest its work after each job. Misbehavior slashes the bond and resets reputation, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds - attack cost scales linearly with the number of sybils. Honest history then accrues slowly, layer by layer like shale, until a violet badge of sustained good conduct lets the agent dock at the wharf of high-value contracts, where one verified identity earns far more than a fleet of cheap throwaways.
